narration: The Never-Ending Circle
This is Hoop Dance. 20th century.
on_screen: Title card: Hoop Dance · USA · 20th century

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Attributed to the Anishinaabe figure Pukawiss, the dance was created to teach animal movements and human values.
Modern hoop dance, which uses multiple hoops, was pioneered in the 1930s by Tony White Cloud, who performed in films such as 'Valley of the Sun' and 'Apache Country'.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is a form of 'entertaining dance' in many tribes, though it retains spiritual significance.
It is used for storytelling, healing ceremonies, and as a competitive cultural heritage event.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dancer performs solo, using small, restrained steps while manipulating hoops around the body.
Hoops are interlocked to form appendages like wings or tails.
Movements are rapid and individualistic, often mimicking animals or natural cycles.
Watch for Animal Mimicry.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Solo dancer moving in clockwise or counterclockwise directions.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is accompanied by drums and flutes.
The tempo varies; some dancers use extremely fast songs with few hoops, while others use 20 or more hoops to a slower, steady drumbeat.
Listen for the Drum, Flute.
The music is characterized by the steady, percussive beat of traditional drums and the melodic accompaniment of flutes, providing a rhythmic foundation for the dancer's rapid movements.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Dancers wear regalia that allows for fluid movement.
Hoops are typically 24 inches in diameter, traditionally made of willow but now often constructed from plastic piping or reeds, decorated with paint and tape.
on_screen: Image gallery: 3 licensed images with attribution
Reconstruction imagery allowed only from the costume notes, labelled 'reconstruction'

scenes.title: The people
narration: Tony White Cloud (founder of modern hoop dance), Kevin Locke, Eddie Swimmer (first World Champion), Quentin Pipestem, Jackie Bird, Ginger Sykes, Jasmine Pickner, Lisa Odjig, and Nakota La Rance.
While pan-Indian in nature, specific tribal traditions exist, such as the healing-oriented hoop dance of the White Mountain Apache.
The dance evolved from traditional storytelling and healing rituals into a modern, competitive show dance.
